Inside, a scrap of paper bore handwriting so faded he had to hold it against the lantern's glow to read it. 'To whoever finds this — I am not lost. I simply chose the sea.' He turned the words over in his mind as the beam swept its eternal arc above him. In thirty years of tending this light, he had pulled many things from the tide: driftwood, nets, once a piano key. He folded the note carefully and placed it on the shelf beside his logbook, wondering whether choosing the sea and being lost were really so different.", "w02": "凌晨四点，城市尚在沉睡。街灯将橙黄色的光晕洒在空旷的柏油路上，偶尔一辆出租车驶过，轮胎碾过积水发出细碎的声响。早点铺的灯已经亮了，蒸笼里白雾升腾，老板娘系着围裙在案板前揉面，动作熟练而安静。远处环卫工人的扫帚划过人行道，沙沙声在寂静中格外清晰。天边泛起一抹极淡的灰蓝，几只麻雀在电线上抖落夜露。整座城市像一个即将醒来的人，呼吸平稳，眼皮微颤，等待第一缕阳光将它彻底唤醒。", "w03": "• Recursion is when a function solves a problem by calling itself with a smaller version of the same problem — like looking up a word in the dictionary and finding the definition uses another word you also need to look up.\n• Every recursive function needs a \"base case\" — a simple version of the problem it can answer right away without calling itself again, so it doesn't keep going forever.\n• Imagine you're in a line of people and you want to know your position: you ask the person in front of you their position, they ask the person in front of them, and so on until the first person says \"I'm number 1\" — then everyone passes the answer back, each adding one."}
